title: Logarithmic Potential, Capacity, and Riesz Decomposition

items.title: Support of a finite Borel measure on the plane
items.statement: For a finite positive Borel measure μ on C, supp μ is the complement of the union of all open sets V with μ(V)=0; it is closed, it is the smallest closed set carrying μ, μ is carried by a compact set exactly when supp μ is compact, and μ≠0 exactly when supp μ≠∅.

references.title: B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes
E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory

items.strategy: Define the support as the complement of the union of all open null sets; use the countable rational-box basis to show that this union is null without any choice principle, so the support is the smallest closed carrier, and record the nonempty, carried-by-compact and compact-support conventions.

items.title: Logarithmic potential and energy of a positive compactly supported measure
items.statement: For a finite positive Borel measure μ of compact support in C set U^μ(z)=∫log(1/|z−w|)dμ(w)∈(−∞,+∞] and I(μ)=∬log(1/|z−w|)dμ(z)dμ(w)∈(−∞,+∞]. Write p_μ=−U^μ=∫log|z−w|dμ(w). For a finite measure without compact support these integrals are defined only when their positive and negative parts are not both infinite.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.strategy: On a fixed compact support the logarithmic kernel has a finite lower bound and is Borel, with +∞ on the diagonal. Integrate its nonnegative shift using Tonelli and subtract the finite constant; the same argument applies to the point potential. State the failure of an unconditional extended integral for arbitrary noncompact finite measures when the near-diagonal and far-tail parts both diverge.

items.title: Robin constant and logarithmic capacity of a compact set
items.statement:
Let $K\subseteq\mathbb C$ be compact and nonempty, and let $P(K)$ be the set of
Borel probability measures on $K$ (def-probability-measure), viewed as
measures on $\mathbb C$ carried by $K$. Every $\mu\in P(K)$ has compact support
contained in $K$, so its logarithmic energy $I(\mu)\in(-\infty,+\infty]$ is the
quantity of def-logarithmic-potential-and-energy; indeed the kernel
$k(z,w)=\log(1/|z-w|)$ is bounded below on $K\times K$: it is $\ge-\log\operatorname{diam}K$
when $\operatorname{diam}K>0$, and $I(\mu)=+\infty$ for the only measure of
$P(K)$ when $K$ is a singleton.

The **Robin constant** of $K$ is

$$V_K:=\inf_{\mu\in P(K)}I(\mu)\in(-\infty,+\infty].$$

The set $P(K)$ is nonempty: it contains the Dirac measure at any point of
$K$ (def-dirac-measure). Put $E_K:=\{I(\mu):\mu\in P(K),\ I(\mu)<+\infty\}$.
If $E_K=\varnothing$, all energies are $+\infty$ and we set $V_K=+\infty$.
Otherwise $K$ is not a singleton, and $E_K$ is a nonempty subset of $\mathbb R$
bounded below by $-\log\operatorname{diam}K$, so thm-infimum-property
gives its real infimum. Set $V_K=\inf E_K$ in this case. Adding the value
$+\infty$ does not change any real lower bound, so this is exactly the
extended infimum displayed above. The **logarithmic capacity** of $K$ is

$$\operatorname{cap}(K):=\begin{cases}\exp(-V_K) & \text{if } V_K<+\infty,\\ 0 & \text{if } V_K=+\infty,\end{cases}$$

with $\exp$ the real exponential function (def-real-exponential-function-and-e).
Thus $\operatorname{cap}(K)\in[0,\infty)$ for every nonempty compact $K$, and for
the empty set one uses the separate convention

$$\operatorname{cap}(\varnothing):=0.$$

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.strategy: Use the finite diameter bound log(1/|z−w|)≥−log diam K for diam K>0; a singleton has only its Dirac law and infinite energy. For K empty use the separate convention. Monotonicity follows by inclusion of admissible probability families.

items.title: Lower semicontinuity of logarithmic potential and energy
items.statement: Let K⊂C be nonempty compact and let μ_n,μ be Borel probability measures on K with μ_n⇒μ. With the Borel logarithmic kernel assigned +∞ on the diagonal, U^μ(z) and I(μ) are unambiguous extended integrals: two Borel kernels agreeing with k off a μ-null set give the same potential, and two agreeing off a (μ⊗μ)-null set give the same energy. Moreover U^μ(z)≤liminf_n U^{μ_n}(z) for every z∈C and I(μ)≤liminf_n I(μ_n). If μ({z})>0 then U^μ(z)=+∞, so for atomic measures the diagonal value is not free. No choice principle is required.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Strict positivity of logarithmic energy for a zero-mass signed charge
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. If μ and ν are compactly supported positive measures of equal mass and finite logarithmic energy, their mixed energy is finite and σ=μ−ν has well-defined I(σ)≥0, with equality exactly when σ=0.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5
Frerick–Müller–Thomaser, A Fourier integral formula for logarithmic energy, Theorem 1.1 and Remark 3.3

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium measure
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subseteq\mathbb C$ be nonempty and compact with $\operatorname{cap}(K)>0$. Then there is exactly one Borel probability measure $\mu_K$ on $K$ with $$I(\mu_K)=V_K=\inf_{\mu\in P(K)}I(\mu)<+\infty .$$ The measure $\mu_K$ is the **equilibrium measure** of $K$. If $\operatorname{cap}(K)=0$ then $V_K=+\infty$, every $\mu\in P(K)$ has $I(\mu)=+\infty$, and no equilibrium measure is asserted. The Axiom of Choice is spent twice: through Countable Choice for the minimizing sequence, and through the weak sequential compactness of probability laws of lem-probability-laws-on-a-compact-metric-space-have-weakly-convergent-subsequences. The energy lower semicontinuity used below is choice-free (thm-logarithmic-energy-well-defined-and-lower-semicontinuous).

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Capacity-polar sets, quasi-everywhere, and subharmonic polar sets
items.statement: Let $K\subseteq\mathbb C$ be compact; call it the **conductor** when it is fixed as the ambient set of a quasi-everywhere statement. Capacity is the logarithmic capacity of def-logarithmic-capacity-compact-set, whose conventions $\operatorname{cap}(\varnothing)=0$ and $\operatorname{cap}(F)>0$ or $=0$ for nonempty compact $F$ are used verbatim. **Capacity-polar sets.** A set $E\subseteq\mathbb C$ is **capacity-polar** when $$\operatorname{cap}(F)=0\qquad\text{for every compact }F\subseteq E .$$ The restriction to compact subsets is deliberate: capacity is defined here for compact sets, so the definition tests $E$ through its compact parts, and a capacity-polar set may be neither compact nor Borel. A compact $F$ is capacity-polar exactly when $\operatorname{cap}(F)=0$, and $\varnothing$ is capacity-polar by the convention $\operatorname{cap} (\varnothing)=0$. A set $E$ is **nonpolar** when it is not capacity-polar, that is, when it contains a compact set of positive capacity. **Quasi-everywhere.** Let $P$ be a property of the points of a compact conductor $K$, that is, a statement $P(z)$ for $z\in K$. One says that $P$ holds **quasi-everywhere on $K$**, abbreviated $P$ holds q.e. on $K$, when there is a Borel capacity-polar set $E\subseteq K$ with $$P(z)\ \text{holds for every }z\in K\setminus E .$$ The exceptional set $E$ is required to be Borel so that the statement has a measurable exceptional carrier; the definition itself asks nothing about the values of $P$ on $E$. If $P$ holds everywhere on $K$ it holds q.e. on $K$, with $E=\varnothing$. A set $N\subseteq K$ is called q.e.-negligible when it is contained in a Borel capacity-polar subset of $K$; a property holds q.e. exactly when it fails on a q.e.-negligible set. **Subharmonic polar sets.** A set $E\subseteq\mathbb C$ is **subharmonically polar** when for every $x\in E$ there are an open set $U_x\ni x$ and a function $u_x$ subharmonic on $U_x$ (def-plane-subharmonic-function) with $$E\cap U_x\ \subseteq\ \{z\in U_x:u_x(z)=-\infty\}.$$ Because subharmonicity on $U_x$ already excludes the function $-\infty$ on a connected component (def-complex-domain), such a $u_x$ is automatically not identically $-\infty$ on any component of $U_x$; the requirement in the literature that the witness be "not identically $-\infty$" is therefore automatic in this convention. If $E$ is contained in the union of a single open set carrying one such witness, the local condition holds with that one function; the definition uses the local form so that unbounded or noncompact $E$ need no global witness.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.strategy: Define capacity-polar through the inner compact capacity: a set is capacity-polar when every compact subset has cap 0. Quasi-everywhere on a compact conductor K means a property fails only on a Borel capacity-polar set. Define subharmonically polar sets locally, by existence of a local subharmonic witness whose -infinity locus covers the set near each point; subharmonicity already excludes the identical -infinity function on components, and no global witness is required for unbounded sets. Keep the two notions separate: the compact-polar equivalence is the following lemma, and no equivalence for arbitrary non-Borel sets is asserted. Record that polarity is inherited by subsets and that the definition is choice-free.

items.title: Maximum principle for a compact logarithmic potential
items.statement: For a finite positive compactly supported μ with μ≠0, if U^μ≤M at every point of supp μ for some real M, then U^μ≤M throughout C.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Frostman inequalities and quasi-everywhere equilibrium equality
items.statement: Assume AC and let K be nonpolar compact with equilibrium μ_K. Then U^{μ_K}(z)≤V_K for every z∈C, and U^{μ_K}(z)=V_K outside a Borel capacity-polar subset of K. The exceptional set may be taken as a countable union of compact zero-capacity sets.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Reciprocity inequality for logarithmic potentials
items.statement: Assume AC. Let K⊂C be compact with cap(K)>0 and equilibrium measure μ_K. For every compactly supported Borel probability measure σ on C, inf_{z∈K} U^σ(z)≤V_K=log(1/cap(K)).

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §1

items.title: Chebyshev constant of a compact planar set
items.statement: For nonempty compact K⊂C and n≥1, let t_n(K)=inf{‖p‖_K:p is a monic complex polynomial of degree n}, where ‖p‖_K=sup_{z∈K}|p(z)|. Define cheb(K)=inf_{n≥1} t_n(K)^{1/n}; set cheb(∅)=0. The following lemma proves that the infimum is also the limit of t_n(K)^{1/n}.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §1

items.strategy: For nonempty compact K, polynomial evaluation and modulus are continuous and bounded, so each sup norm is finite; z^n shows the monic class is nonempty. The infimum and nonnegative nth roots are therefore defined. Leave uniqueness of a best monic polynomial unasserted; the Chebyshev constant only uses the extremal infima.

items.title: The Chebyshev constant is the root limit of monic extremal norms
items.statement: For every nonempty compact K⊂C, t_{m+n}(K)≤t_m(K)t_n(K) for m,n≥1, and therefore lim_{n→∞}t_n(K)^{1/n}=inf_{n≥1}t_n(K)^{1/n}=cheb(K).

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §1

items.title: Monic polynomial lower bounds for the Chebyshev constant and capacity
items.statement: For every nonempty compact K⊂C and every monic complex polynomial p of degree n≥1, ‖p‖_K≥cheb(K)^n. Also ‖p‖_K≥cap(K)^n; hence cap(K)≤cheb(K).

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §1

items.title: Distributional Riesz measure of a plane subharmonic function
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C$ be a plane domain and let $u:\Omega\to[-\infty,\infty)$
be subharmonic on $\Omega$ (def-plane-subharmonic-function); in particular
$u$ is not identically $-\infty$ on any component. Then $u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$
(thm-plane-subharmonic-functions-are-locally-integrable), so for every
compactly supported smooth test function $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ the
Lebesgue integral $\int_\Omega u\,\Delta\varphi\,dA$ converges absolutely: the
support of $\Delta\varphi$ is compact and $\Delta\varphi$ is bounded, so
$\int_\Omega|u\,\Delta\varphi|\,dA\le\|\Delta\varphi\|_\infty\int_{\operatorname{supp}\Delta\varphi}|u|\,dA<\infty$.
The **distributional Riesz functional** of $u$ is

$$\mu_u(\varphi):=\frac1{2\pi}\int_\Omega u\,\Delta\varphi\,dA\qquad(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)),$$

where $\Delta=\partial_x^2+\partial_y^2$ is the Laplacian, $dA$ is area Lebesgue
measure, and $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ is the test space of def-distribution
with the distributional derivative conventions of def-distributional-derivative.
The value is complex in general and is real for real-valued test functions.
The functional $\mu_u$ depends only on the almost-everywhere
representative of $u$: if $u=v$ a.e. then $u\,\Delta\varphi=v\,\Delta\varphi$
a.e. for every test function, so the integrals agree. Linearity in $\varphi$ is
inherited from the linearity of differentiation and integration.

The normalization factor $(2\pi)^{-1}$ is chosen so that, under Countable
Choice (def-countable-choice), a logarithmic point potential has unit
mass at its pole: $\Delta\log|z-a|=2\pi\delta_a$ in the
distributional sense, that is, $\mu_{\log|{\cdot}-a|}=\delta_a$
(thm-minus-laplacian-of-the-fundamental-solution-is-dirac).

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.strategy: Local L¹ integrability makes the formula independent of the a.e. representative of u and gives a distribution. Different test-function coordinates are covered by the distributional derivative definition; positivity and measure representation are not assumed at definition time.
items.proof_strategy: Local integrability of plane subharmonic u makes ∫uΔφ finite for every compactly supported smooth test. Changing u on an area-null set does not change this integral. The two distributional derivative signs cancel in Δu, giving the stated functional and fixing the 2π normalization; positivity and Radon representation are established by the immediately following theorem.

items.title: The distributional Laplacian of a subharmonic function is a positive Radon measure
items.statement: Assume DC. For a subharmonic u on a complex domain Ω with distributional Riesz functional μ_u=(2π)^{−1}∫uΔφ dA: (i) μ_u(φ)≥0 for every real φ∈C_c^∞(Ω) with φ≥0; (ii) there is exactly one positive Radon measure ν on Ω with μ_u(φ)=∫φ dν for all φ∈C_c^∞(Ω). DC is used for the RMK representation and uniqueness; mollification and density use only AC_ω, which DC implies.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Distributional Laplacian of a compact logarithmic potential
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For finite positive compactly supported μ, p_μ=∫log|z−w|dμ(w) is locally integrable, subharmonic on C, harmonic off supp μ, and Δp_μ=2πμ in distributions; equivalently ΔU^μ=−2πμ.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Local Riesz decomposition of a plane subharmonic function
items.statement:
Assume Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C$ be a complex domain,
let $u$ be subharmonic on $\Omega$ in the sense of
def-plane-subharmonic-function, and let $D\subseteq\Omega$ be open with
$\overline D$ compact and $\overline D\subseteq\Omega$. Let
$\mu_u=(2\pi)^{-1}\Delta u$ be the Riesz measure of
def-riesz-measure-subharmonic-function and let
$M$ be the restriction $\mu_u|_D$ of def-restriction-of-a-measure,
extended by zero to $\mathbb C$: explicitly,
$M(A):=\mu_u(A\cap D)$ for $A\in\mathcal B(\mathbb C)$. Then $M$ is a finite positive Borel measure
carried by $D$, and there is a function $h$ harmonic on $D$ with

$$u(z)=h(z)+\int_{\mathbb C}\log|z-w|\,dM(w)\qquad\text{for every }z\in D,$$

the integral $\int\log|z-w|\,dM(w)$ being an element of $[-\infty,+\infty)$
whose value $-\infty$ is allowed. Moreover the pair is unique: if $M'$ is a
finite positive Borel measure carried by $D$ and $h'$ is harmonic on $D$ with
$u(z)=h'(z)+\int_{\mathbb C}\log|z-w|\,dM'(w)$ for every $z\in D$, then
$M'=M$ and $h'=h$.

Dependent Choice is spent through Countable Choice in the Fourier/Radon suppliers, the Weyl lemma, the embedding of locally integrable functions in distributions, the polar-coordinate formula used to compare circle averages, and the selection of radii in step 8.1. The potential and averaging estimates themselves are choice-free.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5
Christian Kuehn, Introduction to Potential Theory via Applications, §2.3 Theorem 2.44

items.title: Compact capacity-zero sets and subharmonic polar loci
items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice (hence Countable Choice). For a compact E⊂C, cap(E)=0 if and only if E is contained in the −∞ locus of a nonidentically−∞ subharmonic function on a neighborhood of E. The equivalence extends to a specified Fσ countable union of such compacts, even when unbounded; no arbitrary non-Borel-set equivalence is asserted.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5
W. Hansen and I. Netuka, On Evans' and Choquet's Theorems for Polar Sets
references.locator: Theorem 1.1 and proof §2.1, printed pp. 2–4; direct shifted-kernel construction is recorded in the owner repair note

items.title: Principle of descent and the logarithmic domination principle
items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice. (a) Principle of descent: if K⊂C is nonempty compact and μ_n,μ are finite positive Borel measures on K with μ_n⇒μ, then U^μ(z)≤liminf_nU^{μ_n}(z) for every z∈C and I(μ)≤liminf_nI(μ_n). (b) Logarithmic domination: if μ,ν are finite positive Borel measures with compact support, μ(C)>0, ν(C)≤μ(C), I(μ)<+∞, and U^μ≤U^ν+c holds μ-a.e. for some c∈R, then U^μ≤U^ν+c everywhere on C. The hypothesis μ(C)>0 is necessary: μ=ν=0, c<0 is a counterexample.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5
T. Bloom and N. Levenberg, Pluripotential Energy
references.locator: Proposition 5.9, printed pp. 21–23, especially the epsilon-maximum domination proof

references.title: V. Guedj and A. Zeriahi, The Weighted Monge–Ampère Energy of Quasi-Plurisubharmonic Functions
references.locator: §1.1, Proposition 1.6 and Corollary 1.7, printed pp. 3–8, strict-contact measure identity

items.title: Green function with a pole at infinity
items.statement:
Let $K\subseteq\mathbb C$ be **compact and nonpolar**, meaning that
$\operatorname{cap}(K)>0$ for the logarithmic capacity of
def-logarithmic-capacity-compact-set; by def-polar-set-and-quasi-everywhere
this is exactly the statement that $K$ is not capacity-polar. Such a $K$ is
nonempty, the complement $\mathbb C\setminus K$ is a nonempty open set, and it
has exactly one unbounded connected component
(thm-complement-of-a-compact-plane-set-has-one-unbounded-component); that
component is written

$$\Omega:=\Omega(K)\subseteq\mathbb C\setminus K .$$

By def-complex-domain, $\Omega$ is a complex domain, and $\Omega\ne\mathbb C$
because $K\ne\varnothing$ is disjoint from it. It is called the **exterior
domain of $K$**. Its boundary $\partial\Omega$ (interior, closure and boundary
in the sense of def-metric-interior-closure-boundary) is a compact subset of
$K$: indeed $\partial\Omega\subseteq\partial(\mathbb C\setminus K)\subseteq K$,
and it is called the **outer boundary of $K$**. Every point of $\partial\Omega$
is a finite point of $\mathbb C$; the point $\infty$ is not part of it.

Since $\operatorname{cap}(K)>0$, the Robin constant
$V_K=\inf_{\mu\in P(K)}I(\mu)$ of $K$ is a real number, $V_K<+\infty$
(def-logarithmic-capacity-compact-set); it is the **Robin constant in the
pole at infinity**. Harmonicity below is that of
def-plane-harmonic-function, and moduli are those of
def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus.

A **Green function of $\Omega$ with pole at infinity and Robin constant
$V_K$** is a function $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ with the following four
properties.

1. **Positive and harmonic.** $g(z)>0$ for every $z\in\Omega$, and $g$ is
   harmonic on $\Omega$.
2. **Logarithmic normalization at infinity.** Writing $\log$ for the natural
   logarithm and $|{\cdot}|$ for the modulus,

   $$g(z)-\log|z|\longrightarrow V_K\qquad\text{as }|z|\to\infty,\ z\in\Omega, $$

   meaning: for every real $\varepsilon>0$ there is a real $r$ such that
   $|g(z)-\log|z|-V_K|<\varepsilon$ for every $z\in\Omega$ with $|z|>r$.
   Because $\Omega$ is unbounded, this condition is never vacuous.
3. **Local boundedness near finite boundary points.** For every
   $\xi\in\partial\Omega$ there is a real $r>0$ with

   $$\sup\{\,g(z):z\in\Omega,\ |z-\xi|<r\,\}<+\infty .$$

4. **Zero boundary limit quasi-everywhere.** There is a Borel capacity-polar
   set $E\subseteq\partial\Omega$ such that

   $$\lim_{\Omega\ni z\to\xi}g(z)=0\qquad\text{for every }\xi\in\partial\Omega\setminus E .$$

   That is, $g$ has boundary limit $0$ **quasi-everywhere on the outer
   boundary**, in the sense of def-polar-set-and-quasi-everywhere applied
   to the compact conductor $\partial\Omega$.

**Notation.** If a Green function with pole at infinity and Robin constant
$V_K$ exists and is unique under properties 1–4, that unique function is
written

$$z\mapsto g_\Omega(z,\infty),\qquad\text{equivalently } z\mapsto g_{\Omega(K)}(z,\infty).$$

Neither existence nor uniqueness is asserted by this definition: they are
conclusions of the theorem that builds the Green function from the equilibrium
potential, and it is only there that the notation $g_\Omega(\cdot,\infty)$ is
licensed.

**Independence from the finite-pole kernel.** Properties 1–4 are stated for an
unbounded exterior domain and normalize the logarithmic term with coefficient
$+1$ and the additive constant $V_K$ at infinity. This is not the published
finite-pole canonical Green kernel $z\mapsto g_\Omega(z,a)$ of
def-green-function-plane-domain, whose pole is a point $a\in\Omega$ and
whose local form is $g_\Omega(z,a)=-\log|z-a|+h(z)$ with $h$ harmonic across $a$. No clause
above is imported from, or reduces to, that kernel; the two are different
objects even on a common domain.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.strategy: For a compact nonpolar K, let Omega be the one unbounded component of C minus K with outer boundary the compact set partial Omega contained in K, and let V_K be the (finite) Robin constant. Define a Green function with pole at infinity and Robin constant V_K as a positive harmonic g on Omega that is normalized by g(z) - log|z| -> V_K as |z| -> infinity, is locally bounded near every finite boundary point, and has boundary limit zero quasi-everywhere on the outer boundary; record that existence and uniqueness are not asserted here and that the notation g_Omega(.,infinity) is licensed only by the later uniqueness theorem, and keep this distinct from the published finite-pole Green kernel.

items.title: Green function at infinity from the equilibrium potential
items.statement: Assume AC. For compact nonpolar K and Ω the unbounded component of C∖K, g_Ω(z,∞)=V_K−U^{μ_K}(z) on Ω in the preceding infinity-pole normalization. It is positive harmonic on Ω, has g(z)−log|z|→V_K at infinity, and tends to zero at every regular boundary point and quasi-everywhere on the outer boundary; no value is imposed at irregular points.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Fekete points and the transfinite diameter of a compact set
items.statement:
Let $K\subseteq\mathbb C$ be compact and nonempty, let $n\ge2$ be an integer, and
write $K^n$ for the $n$-fold product with the product topology. For
$z=(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in K^n$ set

$$\Delta_n(z):=\prod_{1\le i<j\le n}(z_i-z_j),\qquad D_n(z):=|\Delta_n(z)|=\prod_{1\le i<j\le n}|z_i-z_j|\in[0,\infty).$$

The formula for $\Delta_n$ is the Vandermonde product, whose polynomial form in
$n$ indeterminates is def-vandermonde-polynomial; only the numerical
function $D_n$ on $K^n$ is used here. Each factor $(z_1,\dots,z_n)\mapsto z_i-z_j$
is continuous: the projections are continuous for the product topology
(thm-product-universal-property, def-product-topology), and complex
subtraction is continuous since
$|(z-w)-(z_0-w_0)|\le|z-z_0|+|w-w_0|$
(lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws). Finite products and the modulus
preserve continuity
(lem-algebra-of-continuous-real-maps-on-a-space,
lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws); the product $K^n$ of finitely
many compact spaces is compact
(thm-finite-products-of-compact-spaces), and $K^n\ne\varnothing$. Hence
$D_n$ and the composition

$$(z_1,\dots,z_n)\longmapsto D_n(z)^{2/[n(n-1)]}$$

attain greatest values on $K^n$
(thm-extreme-value-metric). The $n$-th **Fekete diameter** of $K$ is

$$\delta_n(K):=\max_{(z_1,\dots,z_n)\in K^n}D_n(z_1,\dots,z_n)^{2/[n(n-1)]}\in[0,\infty),$$

equivalently $\delta_n(K)=\bigl(\max_{K^n}D_n\bigr)^{2/[n(n-1)]}$, because
$t\mapsto t^{2/[n(n-1)]}$ is increasing on $[0,\infty)$ and the root is the
nonnegative one (thm-nth-roots-exist). The exponent
$2/[n(n-1)]=1/\binom n2$ is the reciprocal of the number of unordered pairs, so
that $\delta_n$ scales like a length. A tuple
$z\in K^n$ at which the maximum is attained is an $n$-point **Fekete tuple** of
$K$, and its entries $z_1,\dots,z_n$ are $n$-point **Fekete points**.

To a Fekete tuple $z$ one associates its **monic Fekete polynomial**

$$F_n(Z):=\prod_{j=1}^n(Z-z_j),$$

a monic polynomial of degree $n$ in the conventions of
def-complex-polynomial-degree-and-monic: each factor $Z-z_j$ is monic of
degree $1$, and degrees add and leading coefficients multiply under multiplication over
the integral domain $\mathbb C$ (thm-polynomial-degree-of-a-product-over-a-domain),
by induction on $n$.

The **transfinite diameter** of $K$ is

$$\tau(K):=\inf_{n\ge2}\delta_n(K)\in[0,\infty),$$

an infimum over a nonempty set of nonnegative reals, hence a well-defined real
number (thm-infimum-property, def-infimum). For the empty set one uses
the separate convention $\tau(\varnothing):=0$. Whether the sequence
$(\delta_n(K))_{n\ge2}$ is nonincreasing, and whether $\tau(K)$ is its limit, is
not assumed in the definition.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.strategy: The Vandermonde product D_n is continuous on the compact nonempty product K^n (projections continuous, complex subtraction and the modulus continuous, finite products of continuous real maps), so it attains a maximum; the exponent 2/[n(n-1)] is the reciprocal of the number of unordered pairs, making delta_n an order-independent length and equal to the increasing normalization of max D_n. Fekete tuples are maximizing tuples (existence, not uniqueness). The monic Fekete polynomial F_n(z)=prod(z-z_j) is monic of degree n by the product-degree theorem. tau(K)=inf_{n>=2} delta_n is a well-defined real infimum, with the separate convention tau(empty)=0; monotonicity of delta_n and equality tau=lim delta_n are deliberately not assumed here and are proved in lem-fekete-diameters-decrease. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Monotonicity of normalized Fekete diameters
items.statement: For every nonempty compact K, δ_{n+1}(K)≤δ_n(K) for n≥2, so τ(K)=lim_{n→∞}δ_n(K).

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Fekete–Szegő equality of logarithmic capacity, transfinite diameter, and Chebyshev constant
items.statement: Assume AC. For every compact K⊂C, cap(K)=τ(K)=cheb(K). If K is infinite, then for any sequence of n-point Fekete tuples with associated monic polynomials F_n, lim_{n→∞}‖F_n‖_K^{1/n}=cheb(K)=cap(K). If cap(K)>0, the empirical probability measures of any sequence of Fekete n-tuples converge weakly to the unique equilibrium measure μ_K; moreover, |F_n(z)|^{1/n}→exp(−U^{μ_K}(z)) uniformly on every compact subset of C\K.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

title: Logarithmic Potential, Capacity, and Riesz Decomposition: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Capacity of a disc and its circular equilibrium measure
items.statement: Assume AC. For K=closed D(a,r), r>0, normalized arclength on |z−a|=r is the unique equilibrium measure, U(z)=log(1/r) for |z−a|≤r and U(z)=log(1/|z−a|) for |z−a|≥r, and cap K=r. The same capacity and measure hold for its boundary circle.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Arcsine equilibrium measure and capacity of a segment
items.statement: Assume AC. For a<b, the unique equilibrium measure of [a,b] is dx/[π√((x−a)(b−x))] and cap([a,b])=(b−a)/4; its potential is log(4/(b−a)) on the segment.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Chebyshev extremals and the exact disk Fekete polynomial
items.statement: Assume AC. For the closed disk $K=\overline{D(a,R)}$, $R>0$, $t_n(K)=R^n$ and $\operatorname{cheb}(K)=R=\operatorname{cap}(K)$, attained by $(z-a)^n$. For $K=[-1,1]$, $t_n(K)=2^{1-n}$ and $\operatorname{cheb}(K)=1/2=\operatorname{cap}(K)$, attained by the monic Chebyshev polynomial $2^{1-n}T_n$. For each $n\ge2$, the $n$th roots of unity form an $n$-point Fekete tuple of the closed unit disk and its monic Fekete polynomial is $F_n(z)=z^n-1$. Their empirical measures converge weakly to normalized arclength on the unit circle. On the unit disk, $\|z^n-1\|=2$, so its nth-root norm tends to $1=\operatorname{cheb}(K)$.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §1

items.title: Chebyshev extremal nodes converge to the arcsine equilibrium measure
items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥1 let x_{k,n}=cos(kπ/n), 0≤k≤n, and ν_n=(n+1)^{-1}Σ_{k=0}^n δ_{x_{k,n}}. Then ν_n converges weakly to dx/(π√(1−x²)), the arcsine equilibrium measure of [−1,1]; the x_{k,n} are the extreme points of T_n(x)=cos(n arccos x).

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §1

items.title: Finite and countable planar sets have zero logarithmic capacity
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Every finite or countable E⊂C is capacity-polar in the compact/local sense. Moreover E is contained in the −∞ locus of an explicitly constructed nonidentically−∞ subharmonic function on C.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Two Cantor sets with different logarithmic capacities
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $C\subseteq[0,1]$ be the middle-thirds Cantor set with Cantor measure $\mu_c$ (def-cantor-set, def-cantor-measure). Then $$I(\mu_c)\le 3\log 3<+\infty,\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \operatorname{cap}(C)\ge e^{-3\log 3}=\tfrac1{27}>0 .$$ Let $\ell_n:=e^{-4^n}$ for $n\ge1$ and let $K\subseteq[0,1]$ be the nested binary Cantor set constructed as follows: $K_0=[0,1]$ is one closed cell, and each level-$(n-1)$ cell $[a,a+s]$ is replaced by the two disjoint closed cells $[a,a+\ell_n]$ and $[a+s-\ell_n,a+s]$, with $K_n$ the union of the resulting $2^n$ cells and $K:=\bigcap_{n\ge0}K_n$. Then every Borel probability $\nu$ on $K$ has $I(\nu)=+\infty$, so $V_K=+\infty$ and $\operatorname{cap}(K)=0$. Both $C$ and $K$ are uncountable compact Lebesgue-null subsets of $[0,1]$. Thus Lebesgue measure and cardinality alone do not determine logarithmic capacity.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5

items.title: Riesz measure of a log modulus records the holomorphic zeros
items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C$ be a complex domain and let $f$ be holomorphic on $\Omega$, not identically zero on any connected component of $\Omega$. Put $u:=\log|f|$, subharmonic on $\Omega$ (thm-log-modulus-of-a-holomorphic-function-is-subharmonic), with Riesz measure $\mu_u=(2\pi)^{-1}\Delta u$ (def-riesz-measure-subharmonic-function). Then $$\mu_u=\sum_{a\in Z(f)}\operatorname{ord}_a(f)\,\delta_a,$$ where $Z(f)=\{a\in\Omega:f(a)=0\}$, the integers $\operatorname{ord}_a(f)\ge1$ are the vanishing orders (thm-zero-order-factorization-holomorphic-function) and $\delta_a$ is the unit Dirac measure at $a$ (def-dirac-measure); the sum is a locally finite positive measure on $\Omega$. In particular $\log|f|$ has no Riesz mass on $\Omega\setminus Z(f)$.

references.title: B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5
C. Kuehn, Introduction to Potential Theory via Applications, §§2.3 and 3.4–3.5

items.title: Infinity-pole Green function recovered from a circular conductor
items.statement: Assume AC. For K=closed D(a,r) with r>0, Ω={|z−a|>r}, the normalized infinity-pole Green function is g_Ω(z,∞)=log(|z−a|/r). It equals V_K−U^{μ_K}(z), vanishes on the entire circle, and has g(z)−log|z|→−log r at infinity.

references.title: E. B. Saff, Logarithmic Potential Theory with Applications to Approximation Theory, §§1–3
B. Khoruzhenko, LTCC Potential Theory notes, §§3 and 5
